question: In which of the following mountain ranges will you find the Guru Shikhar peak?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Aravalli.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Guru Shikhar Peak is located in the Arbuda Mountains of Rajasthan.**
 
• **It is the highest point of the Aravalli Range situated at 1,722 meters.**
 
• It is named** Guru-Shikhar or 'the peak of the guru' after Dattatreya, an incarnation of Vishnu, and a cave at the summit contains a temple dedicated to him, plus one dedicated to his mother, Anasuya, wife of sage Atri.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Satpura Range:**

 
 
• It is a part of the **Deccan plateau. It is a series of seven mountains. Hence, called Satpura.**
 
• It runs in an east-west direction south of the Vindhyas and in between the Narmada and the Tapi, roughly parallel to these rivers.
 
• It stretches for a distance of about** 900 km.**
 
• Dhupgarh which is** 1,350 m** high is located near** Pachmarhi on Mahadev Hills.**
 
 
 
• **The Vindhya Range:**
 
 
• It is a complex, discontinuous chain of mountain ridges, hill ranges, highlands, and plateau escarpments in** West-central India.**
 
• The Vindhya range mostly extends through the Indian states of** Gujarat, Rajasthan, and Madhya Pradesh.**
 
 
 
• **​The Karakoram Range:**
 
 
• It is a mountain range spanning the borders of **China, India, and Pakistan, with the northwest extremity of the range extending to Afghanistan and Tajikistan.**
 
• **It is the second-highest mountain range **in the world. It is a part of the complex of ranges including the Pamir Mountains, the Hindu Kush, and the Himalayan Mountains. The Karakoram Highway connects China-Pakistan.
 
• The range has eight mountains with tops over **7,500 meters (24,600 ft) high**.
 
• **Four of these are higher than 8,000 meters (26,000 ft). They are K2, Gasherbrum I, Broad Peak, and Gasherbrum II.**
